course_name_original: INDUSTRIAL ROBOTICS AND LABORATORY OF ROBOTICS I.C. (B033699)
course_name_en: Industrial Robotics and Laboratory of Robotics I.C.
prerequisites: Knowledge of: Geometry and Linear Algebra
Modelling and control of LTI systems
Knowledge of the fundamentals of robotics is desired: kinematics, dynamics, trajectory planning of free motion, sensors and actuators, decentralized and centralized control techniques

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the principles of industrial electrical engineering, electrical machines, industrial robotics, and controls used in industrial plants.
Understanding of applicable techniques and methods and their limitations, including awareness of the non-technical implications of engineering practice.

The ability to solve problems related to resistive and dynamic electrical networks, even in the presence of active components; to select and use electrical machines within mechanical systems, analyzing their performance; to design automatic feedback control systems, also with the aid of computer tools; to understand the operation of manipulator and mobile robots most commonly used in industrial and non-industrial applications; to choose the appropriate drives (electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic) for machines and plants.

The ability to apply one's knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve industrial and specifically mechanical engineering problems, defining specifications and technical, as well as social, health and safety, environmental, and commercial constraints, and to solve them using established methods, thereby implementing engineering projects appropriate to the developed level of knowledge and understanding. The projects may concern products, devices, machines, energy systems, or automatic systems.

The ability to combine theory and practice to solve multidisciplinary engineering problems, taking into account constraints of a non-technical nature, and working in collaboration with other engineers or other professionals typically found in manufacturing companies.
Ability to analyze data and information using known methods and tools, interpret the results, and draw coherent conclusions, also with the support of provided guidance.
Ability to compare different options or solutions to an engineering problem and to contribute to reasoned technical choices, referring to technical standards and standard industry procedures.

Ability to work in a team in a collaborative and coordinated manner, understanding the context of the engineering problem and recognizing the main interdisciplinary implications of the application field.

Ability to organize one's work in compliance with assigned commitments and deadlines, managing available time and resources, realistically assessing one's capabilities, and contributing to the prioritization of activities.
Ability to recognize one's own limitations in knowledge and the need to acquire new skills, identifying appropriate information sources and guided learning opportunities.

Ability to communicate and transfer information, ideas, problems, and solutions in the engineering field to specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, using appropriate language and referring to known application contexts.
Ability to present problems, solutions, analyses, and results in a clear and structured manner through written reports and oral presentations, according to standard methods and formats.
Ability to represent and communicate data, results, and technical solutions graphically, through the preparation of diagrams, graphs, and tables, using established tools and conventions.
Ability to learn and update one's knowledge in the reference engineering area, also independently but predominantly in a guided manner, using established teaching tools and resources.

Ability to find and consult bibliographic sources and technical documentation through the main available resources (libraries, databases, manuals, and digital sources), selecting relevant information with the support of provided guidance.

Ability to learn through teaching methods based on projects and problem-solving (Problem Based Learning – PBL), applying acquired knowledge and tools to case studies and real-world problems of appropriate complexity.

Ability to understand and interpret the basic principles of design, production, and maintenance processes, operating in compliance with quality, safety, and reliability requirements and referring to the main technical and environmental standards (ISO, UNI, ASME, DIN, etc.).
The goal of the course is to invite the pupils to accept the challenge of a practical problem in robotics.

In-depth knowledge of the theoretical and scientific aspects of engineering, both in general and in depth with regard to mechanical engineering, for the identification, formulation, and resolution of complex problems or those requiring an interdisciplinary approach

In-depth knowledge of the theoretical and scientific aspects of mathematics and other basic sciences for interpreting and describing complex engineering problems or those requiring an interdisciplinary approach
Knowledge and use of scientific tools (computer-based and other) specific to the field of design in the context of mechanical engineering
Knowledge of methods for conceiving, planning, designing, and managing complex and/or innovative systems, processes, and services
Knowledge of methods for planning and carrying out highly complex experimental activities for the analysis of components and systems
Knowledge of advanced design tools (mechanical, thermo-fluid dynamics, electrical, or multi-physics) for the modeling and numerical simulation of components or systems
Knowledge of the automation and control sector. Knowledge of mechatronic systems
The ability to communicate and transfer information, ideas, problems, and solutions to specialist and non-specialist audiences
The ability to present problems, solutions, analyses, and results professionally through written reports and verbal presentations
Graphic representation and communication skills (drafting diagrams, graphs, and tables)
The ability to independently analyze data and information, draw objective conclusions, and make consequential decisions
The ability to evaluate different options or solutions to a problem and make informed decisions about one's projects, including on the basis of relevant technical standards

Autonomy in meeting commitments and deadlines, with reference to the ability to allocate time and available resources to meet deadlines, to correctly assess one's own abilities and resources to ensure that commitments are realistic and achievable, and to prioritize activities based on their importance and deadlines
The ability to identify the need for new knowledge
The ability to learn and update knowledge autonomously and continuously in the relevant engineering field
Conducting bibliographic research using the main resources (libraries, scientific databases, etc.)
Project-Based and Problem-Based Learning (PBL): ability to learn through teaching methods based on projects and solving real problems

syllabus_topics: Position and orientation of a rigid body
Kinematics of wheeled and legged mobile robots
Inverse differential kinematics and related algorithms
Properties of the dynamic model of manipulators
Dynamic model in the operational space
Exercises on Linear algebra (Matrices, Vectors, Linear transformations, Eigenvalues and eigenvectors, Bilinear and quadratic forms, Pseudoinverse, Singular value decomposition)
Exercises on Kinematics (Direct and inverse kinematics of some manipulator structures)
Exercises on Differential kinematics (Computation of the geometric jacobian for some manipulator structures)
Exercises on Dynamics (Computation of the dynamic model for some manipulator structures with the methods of Lagrange and Newton-Euler)
Exercises on Planning of trajectories (Algorithm of generation of trajectories with parabolic, cubic, quintic and spline time laws)
Exercises on Motion control (Examples of commercial motion control systems, Laboratory demonstration of a controlled axis)
teaching_methods: Class exercises using Matlab and Simulink (if computer labs available)
Visits to companies producing, integrating, and/or using industrial robots (possibly organized)

assessment_methods.method: Written report on project work (Laboratory of Robotics module)

assessment_rules: The overall exam is evaluated with a final grade based on a written and oral exam for the Industrial Robotics module, and a written report demonstrating sufficient achievement of project work goals for the Laboratory of Robotics module. A negative evaluation (Fail) is given for serious conceptual errors or lack of understanding. A grade of 18–22 is sufficient for elementary knowledge and basic independence. Grades improve with understanding, correct application of knowledge, independent task completion, critical analysis, and originality, up to 29–30 and Honors (Lode).
